title: Narc Pattern
intro: Everyone has some Narc pattern — the pull to protect our position, control outcomes and avoid blame. This check shows how strong that pull is in you right now, across four areas. Answer about how you actually behave, especially in conflict.

questions.text: I like to be the one who decides how things are done.
How others see me matters more to me than I let on.
When a relationship has problems, it's usually mostly down to the other person.
Other people's feelings can seem like an overreaction to me.
It bothers me when plans are changed without my say.
I feel a strong need to be recognised for what I do.
If someone is upset with me, I tend to point out what they did first.
I get impatient when people need a lot of emotional support.
I keep track of what I've done for others and what they owe me.
When I'm criticised, I want to set the record straight.
I bring up past mistakes when I'm in an argument.
I sometimes use what I know about someone to win an argument.
I find it hard to back down once I've taken a position.
I sometimes adjust the story so I come across better.
I often feel let down by people who should have known better.
When I'm upset, it's hard for me to see the situation from the other side.
I'm comfortable letting others make decisions that affect me.
I can admit I was wrong without it bothering me much.
I can name my own part in most conflicts I've been in.
I can usually tell when I've hurt someone, even if they don't say so.

bands.title: Low
bands.text: The Narc pattern has a light hold on you. You can generally let others lead, own your part and see the other side, even in conflict. Watch for the areas below that score higher — that's where the pull still shows under pressure.

bands.title: Moderate
bands.text: The Narc pattern shows up, mostly under pressure. In calm times you share control and see other people clearly; in conflict you're more likely to defend your position, keep score or focus on what the other person did. That's very common — and it's where the most change is available.

bands.title: High
bands.text: The Narc pattern is a strong pull for you. Protecting your position, being seen in the right and staying in control often come before the other person's view — especially when you feel challenged. It probably feels like self-protection from the inside. The people around you are likely to experience it as hard to reach you.

bands.title: Very high
bands.text: The Narc pattern is running much of how you handle people and conflict right now. Control, image and blame are doing a lot of work, and the other person's experience is hard to hold onto when you're under pressure. That doesn't define who you are — patterns can shift — but it's worth taking seriously, and talking it through with someone you trust or a professional can help.

cta.text: Want the full picture? The Awareness Profile maps all four patterns — Narc, Empath, Grounded and Volatile — across 56 questions, with a written report available.

disclaimer: This is a self-reflection tool about behaviour patterns. It is not a test for narcissism or Narcissistic Personality Disorder, and it is not a diagnosis of any condition.
